The brief names a character family but states no poses, cycles, directions or timing, and neither reference shows motion; both retained sources name this gap. The light, dark and busy bands used in the readability criterion are the agent's test set, not the game's backgrounds.

1	# Agent-to-agent asset work
2	
3	Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.
4	
5	## Caller → specialist
6	
7	Supply the smallest complete assignment:
8	
9	| Context | What the specialist needs |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
12	| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
13	| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
14	| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
15	| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
16	| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
17	| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |
18	
19	Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.
20	
21	For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.
22	
23	The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.
24	
25	When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
26	the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
27	criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
28	**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
29	scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
30	Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
31	A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
32	requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
33	also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
34	explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
35	Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.
36	
37	For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
38	when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
39	uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
40	Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
41	from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
42	assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
43	and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
44	claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.
45	
46	When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
47	critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
48	Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
49	message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
50	Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
51	caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
52	that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
53	child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
54	an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
55	foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
56	depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
57	changing the user's global configuration.
58	
59	A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.
60	
61	## Specialist → caller while working
62	
63	Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.
64	
65	Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.
66	
67	Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.
68	
69	Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.
70	
71	## Caller: review a cold continuation
72	
73	A returned continuation proposes what the caller should consume next, even when
74	it carries forward unchanged state or previously accepted work. Review the
75	current note, proposed next operation and literal request/criteria that will
76	govern that operation. Reading source files and validating the store establish
77	inputs for this comparison; they do not establish that its conclusions follow.
78	
79	1. Recover the original brief, adopted decisions and existing authorization from
80	   their actual sources. Open the returned continuation and the full relevant
81	   saved criteria yourself. Compare inherited clauses as well as new ones. Keep
82	   historical acceptance attached to the candidate and contract it evaluated;
83	   an unchanged hash or earlier passing verdict does not establish a clause's
84	   authority for the next work.
85	
86	2. Save a compact caller comparison covering each consequential claim,
87	   carried-forward restriction and claimed consequence of an answer. Use the
88	   specialist's [current-effect worksheet](intake-sample.md#write-the-current-effect-before-the-return)
89	   as the proposed claim set, then independently read its sources and actual
90	   prerequisites. Record **claim or literal criterion; source and locator;
91	   current authority/status; change actually authorized; actual operation
92	   prerequisite; finding and disposition**. Cite the evidence you interpreted,
93	   not the specialist's assurance that it supports the claim. A filled worksheet
94	   is not a passing review. Split mixed-authority clauses and distinguish a
95	   required condition from a source-permitted default or alternative. If a rule
96	   excludes a plausible alternative, identify whether the source excludes it or
97	   the rule belongs to a narrower expert trial. Preserve required outcomes when
98	   correcting an unsupported recipe.
99	
100	3. For each requested answer, independently apply the
101	   [operation-effect check](intake-sample.md#check-what-an-answer-enables): trace
102	   the named task/phase through its outputs, actual or intended contracts and
103	   all linked choices, then its applicable dependency/adoption gates. A missing
104	   contract makes the future choice check conditional; a short current blocker
105	   list does not establish all prerequisites for the proposed operation. Assume
106	   only that answer is supplied. Each other choice keeps its status and scope
107	   unless the answer explicitly adopts it or a cited existing decision already
108	   establishes it. Compare every claimed effect in the question, decision table,
109	   saved note and final response. Matching values or adding an adoption decision
110	   does not confirm other choices. Distinguish a usable contract draft
111	   from task readiness and artwork acceptance. Name the dependencies that remain
112	   without making later production requirements block authorized sample work.
113	
114	4. When this comparison finds a discrepancy, send your own precise finding and
115	   source evidence to the same native specialist. Ask for a corrected current
116	   proposal with an explicit old-to-new explanation, preserving the historical
117	   artifacts and acceptance. Wait for the revision. If the first return is
118	   consistent, record the independent comparison without inventing a correction
119	   round. Do not declare consistency solely because the specialist followed a
120	   checklist, retained earlier bytes or returned a valid state.
121	
122	5. After the last specialist change, reopen the actual final files and current
123	   state, verify their identities and applicable runtime checks, and recheck the
124	   affected claims against the sources. Bind your finding to that final version.
125	   Write your own authored result fields from the reviewed current-effect
126	   statements, not from a predecessor's result. Identify the exact current note
127	   sections you adopt; do not make an old note wholly current by reference.
128	   Reopen your saved JSON and list each consequential field/JSON pointer beside
129	   its checked effect. Compare the literal field, current note and planned final
130	   wording against the source-backed remaining prerequisites and allowed routes.
131	   A copied sentence, matching hash or general gate list cannot establish that
132	   the claimed effect follows. Resolve any required/optional, default/alternative
133	   or conditional-plan contradiction in a new current version, preserving prior
134	   bytes. Return useful saved progress, any still necessary direct question and
135	   the precise step its answer enables. Keep existing authorization and remaining
136	   dependencies explicit; do not convert a partial answer effect into full clearance.
137	
138	## Specialist → caller at completion
139	
140	Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields). For a
141	PLAR-bound assignment, use the [caller view](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md)
142	of the existing handoff operation so production identities and continuation come
143	from saved state. Direct briefs and planning-only work can use the fields below
144	without manufacturing PLAR or production records:
145	
146	- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
147	- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
148	- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
149	- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
150	- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
151	- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
152	- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.
153	
154	When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.
155	
156	Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.
157	
158	Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.
159	
160	The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.
161	
162	For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
163	use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`,
164	`production.continuation.state_hash` as `expect`, and your `details` object. The
165	selected read's top-level `hash` identifies the PLAR file, not production state.
166	CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --path QUEUE --asset ID
167	--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --view caller --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
168	complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
169	Return the caller view and its exact handoff locator; the caller opens the retained
170	file and compares its state identity with fresh focused PLAR. Omitting `--view caller`
171	keeps the existing receipt response. The view does not add acceptance or alter the
172	saved handoff. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
173	Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.
174	Before returning a reviewed open task, check its current nominee and workflow
175	requirements. Saved verdicts on an unselected candidate do not describe the
176	active output. Nominate the intended candidate through normal state authoring
177	when appropriate; preserve unavailable verdicts and leave the task open.
178	
179	`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
180	expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
181	caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
182	`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
183	runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
184	The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
185	does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.
186	
187	Use optional `details.caller` for the bounded ordinary return: summary, artifact
188	and report locators, issues and integration findings, following its closed
189	[contract](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md). Retain complete observations
190	in the other details fields and referenced files. Each declared file reference
191	contains exactly `path`, `sha256` and `role`; the runtime verifies its current
192	confined file bytes before publishing. These checks do not verify the role or
193	judgment you supplied. The caller view distinguishes
194	these authored claims from derived task, acceptance and continuation facts.
195	A missing integration observation stays unreported; an accepted candidate does
196	not manufacture an assignment-status or integration claim. Without `details.caller`,
197	`caller.present` is false and the full details remain retrievable; legacy prose is
198	not automatically summarized.
199	
200	For example, only when the assigned destination inspection remains unperformed:
201	
202	```json
203	{
204	  "status": "partial",
205	  "caller": {
206	    "summary": "Candidate bytes are retained; required destination inspection remains unperformed.",
207	    "integration": {
208	      "status": "not_performed",
209	      "summary": "No destination observation has been made for this assignment."
210	    },
211	    "issues": [
212	      {
213	        "category": "unfinished_work",
214	        "summary": "The assigned destination check has not run.",
215	        "recovery": "Run the assigned destination check, retain its actual evidence and refresh the handoff."
216	      }
217	    ]
218	  }
219	}
220	```
221	
222	Use actual findings and omit inapplicable fields. Summary/recovery text is bounded
223	to 600 characters; artifact, report, issue and integration-evidence arrays each
224	hold at most 12 entries, and the complete caller block at most 8192 compact UTF-8

# Agent-to-agent asset work

Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.

## Caller → specialist

Supply the smallest complete assignment:

| Context | What the specialist needs |
| --- | --- |
| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |

Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.

For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.

The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.

When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.

For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.

When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
changing the user's global configuration.

A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.

## Specialist → caller while working

Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.

Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.

Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.

Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.

## Caller: review a cold continuation

A returned continuation proposes what the caller should consume next, even when
it carries forward unchanged state or previously accepted work. Review the
current note, proposed next operation and literal request/criteria that will
govern that operation. Reading source files and validating the store establish
inputs for this comparison; they do not establish that its conclusions follow.

1. Recover the original brief, adopted decisions and existing authorization from
   their actual sources. Open the returned continuation and the full relevant
   saved criteria yourself. Compare inherited clauses as well as new ones. Keep
   historical acceptance attached to the candidate and contract it evaluated;
   an unchanged hash or earlier passing verdict does not establish a clause's
   authority for the next work.

2. Save a compact caller comparison covering each consequential claim,
   carried-forward restriction and claimed consequence of an answer. Use the
   specialist's [current-effect worksheet](intake-sample.md#write-the-current-effect-before-the-return)
   as the proposed claim set, then independently read its sources and actual
   prerequisites. Record **claim or literal criterion; source and locator;
   current authority/status; change actually authorized; actual operation
   prerequisite; finding and disposition**. Cite the evidence you interpreted,
   not the specialist's assurance that it supports the claim. A filled worksheet
   is not a passing review. Split mixed-authority clauses and distinguish a
   required condition from a source-permitted default or alternative. If a rule
   excludes a plausible alternative, identify whether the source excludes it or
   the rule belongs to a narrower expert trial. Preserve required outcomes when
   correcting an unsupported recipe.

3. For each requested answer, independently apply the
   [operation-effect check](intake-sample.md#check-what-an-answer-enables): trace
   the named task/phase through its outputs, actual or intended contracts and
   all linked choices, then its applicable dependency/adoption gates. A missing
   contract makes the future choice check conditional; a short current blocker
   list does not establish all prerequisites for the proposed operation. Assume
   only that answer is supplied. Each other choice keeps its status and scope
   unless the answer explicitly adopts it or a cited existing decision already
   establishes it. Compare every claimed effect in the question, decision table,
   saved note and final response. Matching values or adding an adoption decision
   does not confirm other choices. Distinguish a usable contract draft
   from task readiness and artwork acceptance. Name the dependencies that remain
   without making later production requirements block authorized sample work.

4. When this comparison finds a discrepancy, send your own precise finding and
   source evidence to the same native specialist. Ask for a corrected current
   proposal with an explicit old-to-new explanation, preserving the historical
   artifacts and acceptance. Wait for the revision. If the first return is
   consistent, record the independent comparison without inventing a correction
   round. Do not declare consistency solely because the specialist followed a
   checklist, retained earlier bytes or returned a valid state.

5. After the last specialist change, reopen the actual final files and current
   state, verify their identities and applicable runtime checks, and recheck the
   affected claims against the sources. Bind your finding to that final version.
   Write your own authored result fields from the reviewed current-effect
   statements, not from a predecessor's result. Identify the exact current note
   sections you adopt; do not make an old note wholly current by reference.
   Reopen your saved JSON and list each consequential field/JSON pointer beside
   its checked effect. Compare the literal field, current note and planned final
   wording against the source-backed remaining prerequisites and allowed routes.
   A copied sentence, matching hash or general gate list cannot establish that
   the claimed effect follows. Resolve any required/optional, default/alternative
   or conditional-plan contradiction in a new current version, preserving prior
   bytes. Return useful saved progress, any still necessary direct question and
   the precise step its answer enables. Keep existing authorization and remaining
   dependencies explicit; do not convert a partial answer effect into full clearance.

## Specialist → caller at completion

Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields). For a
PLAR-bound assignment, use the [caller view](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md)
of the existing handoff operation so production identities and continuation come
from saved state. Direct briefs and planning-only work can use the fields below
without manufacturing PLAR or production records:

- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.

When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.

Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.

Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.

The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.

For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`,
`production.continuation.state_hash` as `expect`, and your `details` object. The
selected read's top-level `hash` identifies the PLAR file, not production state.
CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --path QUEUE --asset ID
--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --view caller --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
Return the caller view and its exact handoff locator; the caller opens the retained
file and compares its state identity with fresh focused PLAR. Omitting `--view caller`
keeps the existing receipt response. The view does not add acceptance or alter the
saved handoff. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.
Before returning a reviewed open task, check its current nominee and workflow
requirements. Saved verdicts on an unselected candidate do not describe the
active output. Nominate the intended candidate through normal state authoring
when appropriate; preserve unavailable verdicts and leave the task open.

`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.

Use optional `details.caller` for the bounded ordinary return: summary, artifact
and report locators, issues and integration findings, following its closed
[contract](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md). Retain complete observations
in the other details fields and referenced files. Each declared file reference
contains exactly `path`, `sha256` and `role`; the runtime verifies its current
confined file bytes before publishing. These checks do not verify the role or
judgment you supplied. The caller view distinguishes
these authored claims from derived task, acceptance and continuation facts.
A missing integration observation stays unreported; an accepted candidate does
not manufacture an assignment-status or integration claim. Without `details.caller`,
`caller.present` is false and the full details remain retrievable; legacy prose is
not automatically summarized.

For example, only when the assigned destination inspection remains unperformed:

```json
{
  "status": "partial",
  "caller": {
    "summary": "Candidate bytes are retained; required destination inspection remains unperformed.",
    "integration": {
      "status": "not_performed",
      "summary": "No destination observation has been made for this assignment."
    },
    "issues": [
      {
        "category": "unfinished_work",
        "summary": "The assigned destination check has not run.",
        "recovery": "Run the assigned destination check, retain its actual evidence and refresh the handoff."
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Use actual findings and omit inapplicable fields. Summary/recovery text is bounded
to 600 characters; artifact, report, issue and integration-evidence arrays each
hold at most 12 entries, and the complete caller block at most 8192 compact UTF-8
JSON bytes. Move detail to linked files instead of truncating obligations.
Integration status is `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, `not_performed` or
`not_in_scope`; omission is not one of those observations.

Follow the returned full-handoff, details and resume locators for exact retrieval.
Read `resume_inline`: the unchanged `resume` is present up to 4096 compact UTF-8
JSON bytes; otherwise `resume_ref` retrieves it in full. It is never rewritten or
truncated. `details_ref` and `resume_ref` identify physical source ranges and JSON
pointers in the same immutable handoff. Use its `path`/`sha256` for the full file.
These facts describe the captured selection; use the returned `refresh` read
after source or state changes, and reconcile the current identities. Read that full resume before acting on its jobs or
recovery instructions. Keep routine responses useful without pasting the complete
criteria audit, request report or tool transcript into the return.

On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and
its originating connection. Resolve pending work, then retrieve/import and review its
actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can
explain later work in prose while linking the exact resumable artifact.

Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.

effect or claimed blocker. Shared prerequisite rows may be referenced rather than
repeated. It is a reasoning aid, not new PIXL syntax or proof of a correct review.

```text
Current operation and answer effects
State/plan identity:
Operation and phase:
Question (or "no owner answer needed for this operation"):
Assume only this answer:

Prerequisite or permitted alternative | Source + locator | Current status | After only this answer | Still required

Current effect sentence:
Remaining prerequisites:
Authorized default/alternative (or none established):
Current carriers: note section; authored result field/JSON pointer; final wording
Prior instruction superseded: note/section + reason (when applicable)
```

1. Fill the rows from the actual source and prerequisite trace above. Keep every
   unasked choice unchanged. Preserve source-defined alternatives: an allowed
   default and an owner-supplied value are alternative routes, not two mandatory
   inputs. An unknown future contract remains conditional.
2. Write the effect sentence from the completed rows. If anything needed for the
   claimed operation remains, name the narrower step available and the remaining
   requirements; do not say the answer clears the operation's gates. Do not treat
   an answer as completion of a prerequisite whose required work or evidence
   remains missing, or as confirmation of an unasked choice.
3. Make this current operation/decision section self-contained. Keep old notes
   for source evidence and unchanged facts, but do not adopt an entire prior
   note as current instructions. Name the reviewed sections still applicable
   and explicitly supersede conflicting instructions in the new note. Preserve
   the older bytes; do not duplicate the whole project history.
4. Build authored `question`, `necessary_for`, `unlocks`, `next` and `blocked_on`
   fields from these fresh checked statements, preserving their conditions and
   alternatives. Do not initialize their meaning from an old result's fields.
   Keep runtime-derived continuation unchanged; put authored explanation beside it.
5. Reopen the saved note and result. At each listed carrier, compare the actual
   words with the worksheet and source: does it promise more, omit a remaining
   requirement, or turn an allowed alternative into a prerequisite? Correct the
   current version before returning it. Matching text alone does not establish
   source support; a correct summary cannot cancel a contradictory field or
   adopted instruction. Use the checked effect in the final response.

Use this check to ask only for information needed by the immediate dependent
operation. Existing source-backed decisions and authorization still apply; later
production requirements do not block an independently useful sample or local
plan. Keep the detailed trace in the note and return the useful next action and
its material remaining dependencies plainly.

## Cold intake handoff

1. Read the complete production profile and this procedure. Start with the saved
   workflow and focused context, then inspect the sources behind claimed blockers.
   Recover owner decisions and authorization separately from the predecessor's
   proposals, visual judgments and measurements. A diagnostic finding remains
   scoped to its tested artifact; it does not decide the owner's aesthetic or
   establish a requirement for a newly authored asset. Preserve earlier reports
   and identify overbroad inferences in the continuation.

2. Save the [current-effect worksheet](#write-the-current-effect-before-the-return)
   in a new continuation note. Include observed/proposed choices with their real
   authority, source and scope; unasked rows keep their status. A diagnostic can
   support a recommendation without deciding for the owner. Keep the current
   operation section self-contained and continue independent useful work.

3. Apply [the operation-effect check](#check-what-an-answer-enables) to the
   next local operation and any later operation the handoff claims to unlock.
   Trace the proposed contract's linked choices even when that contract is not
   yet saved. Keep its remaining phase/adoption dependencies explicit; preserve
   existing authorization and continue independent sample or planning work.

4. Use the checked note to finish with saved progress, a direct concise question
   addressed to the caller, and the exact local operation its answer unlocks.
   A decision list or a statement that the owner should choose does not ask the
   question. If the necessary choices are already supplied, use them and state
   the next operation without asking again. Keep supporting diagnostics in the
   note; carry their scope and authority into any claim repeated in the response.

When the representative sample is accepted and the assignment continues across a family, enter the [family and delivery operation](family-delivery.md). It records the exact nominated sample as the baseline, saves member and destination plans, and declares collective continuity before batch results. Replaced/rejected samples and unknown provider attempts must be reconciled before dependent production; an old artifact's existence is not baseline eligibility.

54	
55	- **Visual roles:** Interpret a colour's role separately from its extent. An accent,
56	  highlight, border or base colour names a relationship in the design; it does not by
57	  itself prescribe the dominant fill, percentage coverage or exclusivity. Make the
58	  requested role perceptible and coherent, then choose its extent using expert judgment.
59	  A token barely visible mark may fail that purpose, but it does not follow that a
60	  mostly neutral treatment with a clear accent is invalid. State any chosen dominance
61	  as a proposal unless the actual brief or approved reference role requires it.
62	- **Transparency and subject construction:** Separate transparent negative space from
63	  opaque components of the subject. A foreground emblem may include a deliberate
64	  plate, badge, outline or backing with transparent exterior; that is different from
65	  an unintended opaque canvas matte. Identify each shape's intended role from the
66	  brief, composition and consumer before judging it. A transparency requirement alone
67	  does not select an outline-free glyph or prohibit every opaque backing shape.
68	
69	- **Shape relationships:** Keep qualitative relationships separate from a preferred
70	  construction. Asymmetry can involve angles, position, thickness, curvature, length
71	  or several of these; it is not synonymous with unequal arm lengths. Judge whether
72	  the actual silhouette conveys the requested symbol and relationship. A conventional
73	  recipe is useful expert guidance, not an exclusive definition of every recognizable
74	  pixel-art version. Attribute and scope the chosen construction without adding it to
75	  the owner's rejection rule unless the source actually requires that construction.
76	
77	- **Pixel craft:** Judge silhouette, cluster shape, selective detail, contrast hierarchy, and motion readability at the intended size. Evaluate ramps and hue shifts against reference art. Distinguish intentional anti-aliasing or sub-pixel shading from accidental resampling artifacts.
78	- **Characters and animation:** Establish consistent volume, anchor points, equipment placement, direction semantics, contact poses, and temporal spacing. A correct frame count alone does not establish motion quality. Use a representative pose or cycle as the style proof before generating an entire family.
79	- **Tiles and environments:** Establish projection, cell geometry, shared boundaries, transition rules, material identity, repeat visibility, and placement conventions. Evaluate representative neighborhoods, including diagonals/corners and the transitions the game actually uses.
80	- **Modular rigs:** Treat attachment coordinates, transform order, occlusion, rotation sampling, and part replacement as integration contracts. Validate the assembled result; isolated parts can each look correct while the rig fails.

82	- **Simulation and rendering:** Keep material cells, sprite texels, rig parts, and lighting samples distinct. Normal response and shadow occlusion require different evidence. Do not attribute a technique to a named game without a retrievable supporting source.

84	## Evidence discipline
85	
86	Label claims as measured, visually inspected, documentation-supported, inferred, proposed, or unverified as appropriate. Local validators prove their implemented checks only. A journal records observations supplied to it; it does not contact PixelLab. A capability description is not authentication. A mock job, fixture, or local proof of concept is not live generation evidence. Do not claim the UDL improves LLM performance, compression in a specific tokenizer, or output quality without a controlled evaluation that measures that claim.
87

1	# Agent-to-agent asset work
2	
3	Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.
4	
5	## Caller → specialist
6	
7	Supply the smallest complete assignment:
8	
9	| Context | What the specialist needs |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
12	| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
13	| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
14	| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
15	| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
16	| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
17	| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |
18	
19	Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.
20	
21	For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.
22	
23	The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.
24	
25	When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
26	the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
27	criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
28	**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
29	scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
30	Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
31	A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
32	requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
33	also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
34	explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
35	Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.
36	
37	For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
38	when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
39	uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
40	Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
41	from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
42	assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
43	and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
44	claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.
45	
46	When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
47	critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
48	Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
49	message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
50	Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
51	caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
52	that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
53	child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
54	an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
55	foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
56	depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
57	changing the user's global configuration.
58	
59	A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.

61	## Specialist → caller while working
62	
63	Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.
64	
65	Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.
66	
67	Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.
68	
69	Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.

71	## Caller: review a cold continuation
72	
73	A returned continuation proposes what the caller should consume next, even when
74	it carries forward unchanged state or previously accepted work. Review the
75	current note, proposed next operation and literal request/criteria that will
76	govern that operation. Reading source files and validating the store establish
77	inputs for this comparison; they do not establish that its conclusions follow.
78	
79	1. Recover the original brief, adopted decisions and existing authorization from
80	   their actual sources. Open the returned continuation and the full relevant
81	   saved criteria yourself. Compare inherited clauses as well as new ones. Keep
82	   historical acceptance attached to the candidate and contract it evaluated;
83	   an unchanged hash or earlier passing verdict does not establish a clause's
84	   authority for the next work.
85	
86	2. Save a compact caller comparison covering each consequential claim,
87	   carried-forward restriction and claimed consequence of an answer. Use the
88	   specialist's [current-effect worksheet](intake-sample.md#write-the-current-effect-before-the-return)
89	   as the proposed claim set, then independently read its sources and actual
90	   prerequisites. Record **claim or literal criterion; source and locator;
91	   current authority/status; change actually authorized; actual operation
92	   prerequisite; finding and disposition**. Cite the evidence you interpreted,
93	   not the specialist's assurance that it supports the claim. A filled worksheet
94	   is not a passing review. Split mixed-authority clauses and distinguish a
95	   required condition from a source-permitted default or alternative. If a rule
96	   excludes a plausible alternative, identify whether the source excludes it or
97	   the rule belongs to a narrower expert trial. Preserve required outcomes when
98	   correcting an unsupported recipe.
99	
100	3. For each requested answer, independently apply the
101	   [operation-effect check](intake-sample.md#check-what-an-answer-enables): trace
102	   the named task/phase through its outputs, actual or intended contracts and
103	   all linked choices, then its applicable dependency/adoption gates. A missing
104	   contract makes the future choice check conditional; a short current blocker
105	   list does not establish all prerequisites for the proposed operation. Assume
106	   only that answer is supplied. Each other choice keeps its status and scope
107	   unless the answer explicitly adopts it or a cited existing decision already
108	   establishes it. Compare every claimed effect in the question, decision table,
109	   saved note and final response. Matching values or adding an adoption decision
110	   does not confirm other choices. Distinguish a usable contract draft
111	   from task readiness and artwork acceptance. Name the dependencies that remain
112	   without making later production requirements block authorized sample work.
113	
114	4. When this comparison finds a discrepancy, send your own precise finding and
115	   source evidence to the same native specialist. Ask for a corrected current
116	   proposal with an explicit old-to-new explanation, preserving the historical
117	   artifacts and acceptance. Wait for the revision. If the first return is
118	   consistent, record the independent comparison without inventing a correction
119	   round. Do not declare consistency solely because the specialist followed a
120	   checklist, retained earlier bytes or returned a valid state.
121	
122	5. After the last specialist change, reopen the actual final files and current
123	   state, verify their identities and applicable runtime checks, and recheck the
124	   affected claims against the sources. Bind your finding to that final version.
125	   Write your own authored result fields from the reviewed current-effect
126	   statements, not from a predecessor's result. Identify the exact current note
127	   sections you adopt; do not make an old note wholly current by reference.
128	   Reopen your saved JSON and list each consequential field/JSON pointer beside
129	   its checked effect. Compare the literal field, current note and planned final
130	   wording against the source-backed remaining prerequisites and allowed routes.
131	   A copied sentence, matching hash or general gate list cannot establish that
132	   the claimed effect follows. Resolve any required/optional, default/alternative
133	   or conditional-plan contradiction in a new current version, preserving prior
134	   bytes. Return useful saved progress, any still necessary direct question and
135	   the precise step its answer enables. Keep existing authorization and remaining
136	   dependencies explicit; do not convert a partial answer effect into full clearance.

138	## Specialist → caller at completion
139	
140	Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields). For a
141	PLAR-bound assignment, use the [caller view](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md)
142	of the existing handoff operation so production identities and continuation come
143	from saved state. Direct briefs and planning-only work can use the fields below
144	without manufacturing PLAR or production records:
145	
146	- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
147	- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
148	- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
149	- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
150	- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
151	- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
152	- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.
153	
154	When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.
155	
156	Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.
157	
158	Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.
159	
160	The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.
161	
162	For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
163	use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`,
164	`production.continuation.state_hash` as `expect`, and your `details` object. The
165	selected read's top-level `hash` identifies the PLAR file, not production state.
166	CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --path QUEUE --asset ID
167	--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --view caller --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
168	complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
169	Return the caller view and its exact handoff locator; the caller opens the retained
170	file and compares its state identity with fresh focused PLAR. Omitting `--view caller`
171	keeps the existing receipt response. The view does not add acceptance or alter the
172	saved handoff. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
173	Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.
174	Before returning a reviewed open task, check its current nominee and workflow
175	requirements. Saved verdicts on an unselected candidate do not describe the
176	active output. Nominate the intended candidate through normal state authoring
177	when appropriate; preserve unavailable verdicts and leave the task open.
178	
179	`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
180	expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
181	caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
182	`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
183	runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
184	The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
185	does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.
186	
187	Use optional `details.caller` for the bounded ordinary return: summary, artifact
188	and report locators, issues and integration findings, following its closed
189	[contract](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md). Retain complete observations
190	in the other details fields and referenced files. Each declared file reference
191	contains exactly `path`, `sha256` and `role`; the runtime verifies its current
192	confined file bytes before publishing. These checks do not verify the role or
193	judgment you supplied. The caller view distinguishes
194	these authored claims from derived task, acceptance and continuation facts.
195	A missing integration observation stays unreported; an accepted candidate does
196	not manufacture an assignment-status or integration claim. Without `details.caller`,
197	`caller.present` is false and the full details remain retrievable; legacy prose is
198	not automatically summarized.
199	
200	For example, only when the assigned destination inspection remains unperformed:
201	
202	```json
203	{
204	  "status": "partial",
205	  "caller": {
206	    "summary": "Candidate bytes are retained; required destination inspection remains unperformed.",
207	    "integration": {
208	      "status": "not_performed",
209	      "summary": "No destination observation has been made for this assignment."
210	    },
211	    "issues": [
212	      {
213	        "category": "unfinished_work",
214	        "summary": "The assigned destination check has not run.",
215	        "recovery": "Run the assigned destination check, retain its actual evidence and refresh the handoff."
216	      }
217	    ]
218	  }
219	}
220	```
221	
222	Use actual findings and omit inapplicable fields. Summary/recovery text is bounded
223	to 600 characters; artifact, report, issue and integration-evidence arrays each
224	hold at most 12 entries, and the complete caller block at most 8192 compact UTF-8
225	JSON bytes. Move detail to linked files instead of truncating obligations.
226	Integration status is `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, `not_performed` or
227	`not_in_scope`; omission is not one of those observations.
228	
229	Follow the returned full-handoff, details and resume locators for exact retrieval.
230	Read `resume_inline`: the unchanged `resume` is present up to 4096 compact UTF-8
231	JSON bytes; otherwise `resume_ref` retrieves it in full. It is never rewritten or
232	truncated. `details_ref` and `resume_ref` identify physical source ranges and JSON
233	pointers in the same immutable handoff. Use its `path`/`sha256` for the full file.
234	These facts describe the captured selection; use the returned `refresh` read
235	after source or state changes, and reconcile the current identities. Read that full resume before acting on its jobs or
236	recovery instructions. Keep routine responses useful without pasting the complete
237	criteria audit, request report or tool transcript into the return.
238	
239	On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
240	requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and
241	its originating connection. Resolve pending work, then retrieve/import and review its
242	actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can
243	explain later work in prose while linking the exact resumable artifact.
244	
245	Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.
